Signs of the World

Roundabout ahead

History

In 1966, the United Kingdom established the first rules for roundabouts, requiring entering traffic to give way to traffic already circulating. The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends the modern circular arrow symbol.

Adoption

Most of Europe uses the standard triangle, as do countries like South Africa. The United States, Canada, Mexico, Australia, New Zealand and most of Central and South America use a yellow diamond. Outliers like Japan style the sign like a mandatory sign.
